articles.title_orig: Column | I saw the future of driving in Mexico. It’s off-limits to Americans.
articles.title_zh: Column | I saw the future of driving in Mexico. It’s off-limits to Americans.
articles.content_orig:
The unstoppable advance of Chinese automakers into the Mexican market—which continues to see record sales volumes —has dispelled all doubt: they’re here to stay, and it’s only a matter of time before they begin assembling vehicles in the country.
Their motivation lies not only in consolidating their presence in Mexico and the rest of Latin America, but also in meeting, as much as possible, the requirements necessary to export their products to the United States in the event that the market eventually opens up to these brands.
One of the automakers with a global presence that is already acting in anticipation of the inevitable is Nissan, the sales leader in Mexico by volume, whose executives estimate that its Chinese competitors will begin manufacturing cars here within three years, while their entry into the U.S. market will eventually occur, though “not before five years.”
This warning was recently issued by Christian Meunier, the executive in charge of Nissan’s operations throughout the Americas, during a conference in Tokyo where he explained that the consolidation of Chinese brands in Mexico “will trigger fierce price competition that will force Nissan and other traditional manufacturers to cut costs immediately or risk losing market share,” according to a report by AutoNews .
Meunier added that the Japanese automaker has already begun restructuring its costs and product development to prepare for this new wave of rivals.
“We have a very ambitious plan in Mexico, especially to reduce costs and be able to compete with Chinese manufacturers when they localize their production—which will likely happen in the next two or three years—so we must be prepared,” he emphasized.
One of the first measures implemented by Nissan was the introduction to the Mexican market of a hybrid pickup produced by its partner, Zhengzhou Nissan Automobile Co.
The Chinese Onslaught in Numbers
With this decision, the Tokyo-based automaker joins an ever-growing group of automotive companies—such as Ford, General Motors (GM), and Stellantis—that are leveraging production capacity through joint ventures in China to compete in the local market with models imported from that region.
This trend has led to a situation where, by the third quarter of this year, nearly 30% of the vehicles sold in the Mexican automotive market originated from a Chinese assembly plant, regardless of whether they bear the emblem of a Chinese brand or that of a U.S. or European company.
Official figures from INEGI indicate that as of the end of September, China-based brands delivered 130,488 units in the country. However, it is worth noting that this data excludes at least four competitors that do not report their monthly results to the government agency, including BYD, the Chinese automaker that leads in sales in the domestic market according to unofficial estimates.
Experts estimate that total deliveries by Chinese-origin brands in Mexico amounted to 206,679 vehicles in the first nine months of the year. However, to this volume must be added the sales of models imported from China by other global brands—a figure that exceeds 149,000 units, according to INEGI.
This results in a total of nearly 356,000 Chinese-made vehicles sold in the country, while actual sales volume for the period in question would amount to just over 1,220,000 vehicles. Based on these estimates, the market share of vehicles manufactured in China—regardless of brand—stands at 29.2% of the total.
Nissan and the other global brands will be joined by Volkswagen, which confirmed in late September that the first units of the Lamando L sedan destined for the Mexican market have already rolled off the assembly line at its partner SAIC Volkswagen and are on their way, with plans to be displayed at dealerships across the country before the end of the year.

articles.title_orig: Israel election latest: Turnout highest in decades as Netanyahu fights to keep power
articles.title_zh: Israel election latest: Turnout highest in decades as Netanyahu fights to keep power
articles.content_orig:
Almost 45 percent of Israeli voters had cast a ballot by mid-afternoon on Tuesday, according to Israel’s Central Elections Committee, marking the highest election turnout by 2pm (12:00 GMT) in 50 years.
The figure was 6 percent higher than at the same time in the last elections in 2022.
Mitchell Barak, a pollster and former aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told Al Jazeera that voter turnout “is really high and that’s good”.
“I think … it will probably pass its historic peak in ‘73 – when Israel was also involved in a huge war – so draw what conclusion from that you will,” he added.
The election is largely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s handling of the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks and the wars that followed, the most intense period of combat for Israel since the 1973 surprise military campaign by Egypt and Syria.
“Those numbers are going to help the incumbent parties,” Barak said, “as the 3.25 percent threshold a party needs to get into the Knesset remains, the number of votes you need to meet that threshold increases dramatically.”
Israeli officials noted that several polling stations had faced exceptionally long lines, which were attributed to high voter turnout despite rainy and blustery weather in parts of the country, and a flood warning in some areas.
In a message more than five hours after polls opened, Netanyahu urged supporters to vote, saying turnout was high among his opponents on the left and among Palestinian citizens of Israel, about a fifth of the population.
“We need it to be high too. You all need to stream to the polls,” he said. “This is a fateful moment.”
Netanyahu had repeatedly warned supporters of the prospect of high turnout among Palestinian citizens in Israel ahead of the vote, seeking to mobilise his base under the slogan “the right or Palestine”.
Those voters were casting ballots in “unprecedented” numbers, Palestinian candidate Ahmed Tibi said.
Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot have ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, although some possible scenarios envision them propping up a minority government to ensure Netanyahu is removed from office.
Meanwhile, an Israeli rights group has filed a complaint with the country’s election commission warning that widespread delays could be suppressing the vote among Israeli Palestinians.
Though delays could be a result of high voter turnout, the Association for Civil Rights in Israel (ACRI) said in its complaint to the Central Elections Committee that delays had been reported in at least 18 communities. It asked the committee to investigate “whether these delays are deliberate.”
The ACRI also reported “a large presence” of police and National Guard officers at a polling station in the Negev Desert, raising concerns that officers were using crowd control as a pretext to prevent people from entering to vote.

articles.title_orig: Finland and Norway Hold ‘Frank’ Call With Putin on Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Finland and Norway Hold ‘Frank’ Call With Putin on Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Norway and Finland say they are not acting on behalf of other European leaders
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".
After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.
The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.
Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", StÃ¸re said.
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".
StÃ¸re added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
He - like Stubb and StÃ¸re - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.
Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push
StÃ¸re said all their allies had been informed of the call ahead of time.
Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "very sceptical" of Tuesday's dialogue, telling Danish broadcaster DR, it had not been "co-ordinated with any of the rest of us".
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates, was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US, Ukraine and its European allies have been souring since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia - allowing it to export oil to the US.
But last week, Stubb, StÃ¸re and Zelesnky met Witkoff in the Norwegian capital, before the US special envoy travelled on to St Petersburg to meet Putin.
Following the talks, Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to resume three-way negotiations that Russia had stopped for months.
After speaking to the two Nordic leaders, Zelensky said part of their discussions with Putin had centred on November's trilateral talks to be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky said he had discussed with them "various formats for our engagement with partners in Europe that could be useful in further supporting diplomacy, our defense, and our shared security".
Stubb and StÃ¸re are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
As the US administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the European Union of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".

articles.title_zh: Lula’s win in Brazil deals blow to Trump’s Latin America push: former China envoy
articles.content_orig:
Brazilian leader’s re-election described as representing ‘major setback’ for US president’s effort to assert American primacy in region
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s re-election marks a turning point for Latin America and US-Latin American relations, said Chile’s former top envoy to China, who predicted a slowing of Washington’s regional push.
Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, defeated Flavio Bolsonaro – a Brazilian senator, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro and ally of US President Donald Trump – in Sunday’s run-off, winning 51.8 per cent of the vote to secure a historic fourth non-consecutive term.

articles.title_orig: Why did Kylian Mbappé apologize to China? Mao Zedong controversy explained
articles.title_zh: Why did Kylian Mbappé apologize to China? Mao Zedong controversy explained
articles.content_orig:
A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over MbappÃ©'s comments on a "Chinese dictator"
Kylian MbappÃ© has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.
MbappÃ© had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.
The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.
"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,"  MbappÃ© said in a statement.
"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."
Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian MbappÃ©'s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".
The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.
A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.
Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like MbappÃ©.
The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's AurÃ©lien TchouamÃ©ni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, MbappÃ© does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".
The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".
Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.
But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator".
Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".
Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.
Weibo users are recirculating the clip by blurring the meme and redacting references to Mao
Chinese fans have been criticising MbappÃ© â who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements â of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public".
"International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," reads another  comment on Weibo.
As the anger online grew louder, Chinese brands began to cut ties, although they did not explicitly refer to the video.
The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".
Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."
According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV's news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches, Chinese media reported on Tuesday. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs that play in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team with 36 league titles.
China's foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."
MbappÃ© has a significant commercial presence in China
China is a major market for international sports stars and homegrown brands have signed multimillion-dollar endorsement contracts with MbappÃ©, Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, and NBA player Stephen Curry.
By 14:00 local time on Tuesday, five of the top 10 trending topics on Weibo centered on MbappÃ©, with the hashtag "multiple brands terminate partnerships with MbappÃ©" topping the list.
"Don't ever come to China," read one of the top comments on Weibo.
Mao founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s.
His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party.
His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach.
So jokes or memes about Mao are seen not just as an insult to the party but also its closely-guarded narrative about the country's past.
MbappÃ© has said some of the memes "reveal a lack of political and human awareness"
It's unclear when the MbappÃ© meme involving Mao began but his nickname, "the dictator", has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online.
MbappÃ© is widely regarded as one of the best footballers in the world and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture and business.
In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname.
France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling MbappÃ© Mobut â a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.
In an interview with France Football in September, MbappÃ© acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people".
"There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history," he said.
"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life."
Additional reporting by Fan Wang and Osmond Chia

articles.title_orig: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.title_zh: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.content_orig:
Far-right senator banned from leaving country as supreme court judge’s ruling cites money-laundering case
The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro was banned from leaving Brazil and ordered to surrender his passports just hours after his dramatic loss in the presidential election to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva .
The ruling was issued by Alexandre de Moraes, the same supreme court justice who oversaw the trial of the senator’s father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, for attempting a coup.
Bolsonaro posted a video saying the decision was based on an interview his brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, gave last Friday urging his brother to leave Brazil if he lost the election.
On Monday night, Bolsonaro’s party issued a statement acknowledging the election result, saying: “We recognise the presidential result proclaimed by the electoral court, but believe that the questions raised need to be properly clarified through a balanced and democratic political debate.”
Bolsonaro, like his father four years ago, has still not conceded defeat to Lula.
The court’s brief ruling regarding his passport only refers to a criminal case in which the federal police are investigating Flávio Bolsonaro over his possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme . The ruling orders him not to have any contact with his friend Willer Tomaz, a lawyer linked to betting companies that police suspect were being used to launder about £680m.
It also cancelled all of Bolsonaro’s passports, including the diplomatic one he holds as a congressman, and ordered him to hand them over within 24 hours.
Bolsonaro was the first to speak publicly about the matter, before Brazilian media were even aware of the judge’s decision.
In a video posted on social media, he said he had just left a visit to his father, who is under house arrest in Brasília, when “Lula’s federal police were at his door and in the middle of the street, and I was served with an order to hand over my passports and I am also prohibited from leaving the country”.
He added that, although his brother – who is in self-imposed exile in the US – told a US podcast on Friday that he favoured the senator leaving Brazil if he lost the election, “I never said that”.
When his Senate term ends early next year, Bolsonaro will be out of public office for the first time in 24 years, and therefore without the special immunity afforded to officeholders.
He is under investigation in another criminal case, too, over what happened to the £20m he was captured on tape asking a disgraced banker accused of corruption to provide for a biopic about his father.
The Folha de S Paulo newspaper reported that Flávio Bolsonaro had been persuaded to drop his plan to seek to annul the election, which he had announced after the result was declared on Sunday night.
Bolsonaro had claimed that the two-hour extension of voting – intended to allow voters who had been unable to access the mandatory free public transport to cast their ballots – had harmed the election, despite the fact that his own campaign had also argued for an extension.
According to the newspaper, allies and lawyers told him his argument was legally weak.
Bolsonaro had still not publicly reversed his demand for an annulment, and in the same video he said he would file another case to have Lula’s ticket disqualified over alleged abuse of economic power, a similar case to others his legal team brought during the campaign.

articles.title_orig: Iran talks Middle East security, urges region to get US influence out
articles.title_zh: Iran talks Middle East security, urges region to get US influence out
articles.content_orig:
Footage from a polling station in Rio de Janeiro showed electoral officials retrieving the voting results reports and disconnecting the machines after the first round of voting on Oct. 4, 2026. (Reuters)
SAO PAULO, Brazil— About 125 million Brazilians voted Oct. 4 on machines that print no paper ballots. Less than four hours after polls closed, the country knew its presidential election was headed to a runoff between conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva .
That process has been in place for over three decades, and Brazilians have become accustomed to its speed, simplicity, accuracy and routine. The system is robustly audited, completely disconnected from the Internet, and is the largest digital voting system deployed on the planet.
Eleven days before the U.S. midterms, Brazil’s system, analysts say, could offer Americans a more secure way to vote.
The system has been widely praised and was also mentioned in President Donald Trump’s 2025 executive order on elections , where he cited Brazil’s biometric voter identification as an example. Yet Brazil’s count runs partially on the kind of paperless machines that the president has vowed to scrap.
STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS
Election workers prepare and seal electronic voting machines ahead of the upcoming general elections in Brasilia, Brazil, on Sept. 23, 2026. (Mateus Bonomi/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Over the years, Brazil merged federal, state and municipal databases into a digital voting record, whereby voter identity, eligibility and single ability to vote can (and usually must) be verified biometrically. Nearly 9 in 10 voters unlock the machines with a fingerprint.
Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, or TSE, which designs the machines and oversees elections, says there has been no proven fraud since their 1996 debut. The 499,248 machines used on Oct. 4 never connected to the internet. Their software was open to inspection by parties, universities and watchdogs for 11 months before being digitally signed and sealed in public. Last December, the Brazilian government invited a record 149 outsiders to try to break the system; evaluators concluded nothing they found could alter results or reveal how anyone voted.
An electronic voting machine at a Regional Electoral Court (TRE) facility in Brasilia, Brazil, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (Ton Molina/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
On election day, randomly drawn machines are fed paper ballots on camera as federal auditors and foreign observers watch and specifically track results.
Meanwhile, at closing, every machine used at every polling station prints its tally, which is then posted in front of the polling place with a QR code, so anyone can check it against the national count. In an email to Fox News Digital, TSE said each file’s digital signature "confirms that the result was produced by the electronic voting machine registered for that polling station."
Karina Stange Calandrin, a political scientist and professor at Instituto Brasileiro de Mercado de Capitais (IBMEC), says the system combines three traits rarely found together: voting is electronic, votes hashed to voter eligibility are stored locally in the machine and tallying is automated.
"It is an extremely secure and safe system. The machines never connect to the Internet and even the central database system used to transmit tallied votes to TSE must match results issued physically and locally by each individual machine without human interference," she said. Corrupting it, she added, would require breaking the seal of each machine and installing software that wouldn’t match the TSE’s version, automatically disqualifying its tally — a scale of collusion so large that it "simply could not pass undetected."
COLOMBIA'S 'EL TIGRE' SECURES PRESIDENCY AS LEFTIST RIVAL FINALLY CONCEDES DEFEAT
Brazil's right-wing senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party (PL) gestures next to federal deputy and candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, Douglas Ruas (L) during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in Campo Grande neighborhood, in the western zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026. (Douglas SHINEIDR / AFP via Getty Images)
The machines passed their toughest political test in 2022, when former President Jair Bolsonaro , now serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to overturn his 2022 defeat, spent years attacking their credibility without evidence. Bolsonaro is presently serving time under house arrest.
This year, for the first time, a Bolsonaro appointee ran the TSE: Justice Kassio Nunes Marques. Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, finished first with 47% to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The machines at the center of the senior Bolsonaro’s controversy may yet hand victory to his son.
Florencia Ferrer, CEO of e-stategiapublica, which has audited elections in 17 countries, has no doubt the Brazilian system is the most modern and secure in the world. "In India votes are electronic, but each voter gets a printed version of their vote to take home, which weakens voter safety and augments coercion rates," she says, adding that Estonia’s internet voting and the Philippines’ electronically tallied paper ballots carry their own risks.
An engineer from the University of São Paulo’s Polytechnic School who audited the machines in 2014, and declined to be named due to the sensitive nature of his work, agreed. "While no system is completely infallible... we have found no traces of tampering, wrong-doing or malicious intent," he told Fox News Digital.
Still, some defend higher scrutiny. Security researchers say a clean record is not proof enough, and the Carter Center said voters should at least see a printed version of their ballot deposited into a separate area of the machine; otherwise, results integrity rests on software alone. Germany’s top court ruled in 2009 that voters must be able to check their ballot without expert help, effectively barring a Brazilian-like system.
Brazil’s machine has traveled mostly on loan to countries in Latin America , Africa and Asia. Paraguay adopted it permanently in 2006, with machines that now print each individual vote.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Brazil's President and presidential candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (C) waves next to Vice-President Geraldo Alckmin (L) and to his candidate for São Paulo's governor, Fernando Haddad during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in São Paulo, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026, (Luis Robayo/AFP Via Getty Images)
"It’s obvious Washington and the remainder of the U.S. are way behind both technology as well as security when it comes to polling on voting day," Ferrer said. U.S. elections are run in thousands of local jurisdictions under 50 sets of state rules and about 30% of 2024 ballots came by mail , which is slower to process. Brazil has one national election authority, compulsory voting and no mail-in ballots.
Brazilians will vote this coming Sunday on Oct. 25. The winner is expected to be known and certified in under five hours.
"The question is not whether Brazil has invented a perfect voting machine. No voting system is perfect. It is whether democracies can combine the speed and consistency of digital tabulation with independent verification, public scrutiny and rules that citizens across the political spectrum have reason to trust," Ferrer said.
Solly Boussidan is an international journalist covering Latin America for Fox News Digital. He has previously covered international affairs, war, finance and travel for several U.S. and international outlets. He is currently based in Brazil.

articles.title_orig: Boeing’s Earnings Miss Shows Progress. The Market Will Decide If It’s Enough.
articles.title_zh: Boeing’s Earnings Miss Shows Progress. The Market Will Decide If It’s Enough.
articles.content_orig:
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected becuase of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock was down about 9% during the call.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier.
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

articles.title_orig: S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher as oil pulls back ahead of Fed decision
articles.title_zh: S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher as oil pulls back ahead of Fed decision
articles.content_orig:
NEW YORK (AP) — Wall Street is ticking higher Tuesday as stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry support the market, at least for now.
The S&P 500 rose 0.5% and pulled within 1.3% of its all-time high set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 27 points, or 0.1%, as of 11 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.9% higher.
The majority of stocks within the S&P 500 were falling, but gains for several influential AI stocks made up for that. Such stocks have been swerving for weeks on worries about whether their boom is under threat because of how expensive it’s become for companies to borrow money to build data centers and buy more AI chips.
Broadcom climbed 3.3% after announcing a $63 billion financing deal where several Wall Street firms will help Anthropic get access to Broadcom's XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions.
Elsewhere in the industry, Advanced Micro Devices rose 4% and was one of the strongest forces pushing up on the S&P 500 after Broadcom. CoreWeave, a company that’s borrowed money to buy AI chips that it rents out to customers over the cloud, rose 5.2%, though it’s been careening between big gains and losses within each of the past few days.
General Motors climbed 6.3% after saying it’s moving its stock from a listing on the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq. The automaker said the Nasdaq, which is home to several of the world’s biggest technology stocks, is a fit for its tech-driven strategy. The move could also allow GM to join the Nasdaq 100 index, which would force investment funds that mimic the index to buy it.
GM began trading on the NYSE in 1911.
JetBlue Airways flew 20% higher even though it reported a larger loss for the summer than analysts expected. CEO Joanna Geraghty said the company expects to return to making sustained operating profits next year and to deliver at least $1 in earnings per share in 2028.
Investors may have been bracing for something worse after the airline’s stock came into the day with a loss of nearly 48% for the year so far.
Another travel company, Royal Caribbean Group, also helped lead the market and rose 7.5%. The cruise operator delivered a stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected, while raising its forecast for profit over the full year.
Companies overall are under pressure to deliver big growth in profits. Expectations are high among financial analysts and investors, and that’s what allowed their stock prices to run to records recently despite high inflation, high interest rates and other concerns weighing on the market.
It takes reporters, editors, and resources to do this work right. Your donation keeps that work alive.
Boeing fell 9.4% after reporting a larger loss for the latest quarter than analysts expected.
Hilton Worldwide Holdings sank 2.8% after reporting weaker revenue for the summer than analysts expected. It also gave a range as a forecast for profit in the final three months of the year whose midpoint fell below analysts' expectations. The hotel company said it expects to see “increased impact from the Middle East” during the quarter.
Sherwin-Williams fell 1.6% after delivering a weaker profit than analysts expected. High mortgage rates have helped chill the housing industry, which in turn pressures demand for the paints and coatings Sherwin-Williams sells.
“Customer sentiment and the leading indicators we track point to muted demand over the remainder of the year and into 2027,” CEO Heidi Petz said. At the same time, her company is dealing with inflation pushing up its costs for raw materials.
Confidence among U.S. shoppers has tumbled recently as pressure keeps building on them from high inflation. But a report on Tuesday said that U.S. consumer confidence improved in October, when economists expected further weakening.
In the bond market, Treasury yields held relatively steady a day before the Federal Reserve is scheduled to announce its latest decision on interest rates. The Fed last month hiked the fed funds rate for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing inflation, but the widespread expectation on Wall Street is that it will hold rates steady this time.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 4.98% from 5.00% late Monday.
Helping to keep yields in check was a drop for oil prices. The price for a barrel of Brent crude fell 1.2% to $109.43.
In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. Stocks jumped 3.1% in Seoul and fell 1.3% in Shanghai for two of the bigger moves.
AP Writers Elaine Lai and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
United Parcel Service ( UPS ) stock rose 2% on Tuesday after the courier posted third quarter results and raised its full-year guidance, signaling solid demand during the upcoming holiday season.
Revenue is expected to come in at $92.6 billion this year, up from a prior forecast of $91.2 billion. UPS also increased its adjusted earnings guidance.
Despite inflation pressures and high diesel costs, UPS is optimistic heading into the last few months of the year.
"US consumers remain resilient and the outlook for holiday demand is strong," CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's earnings call.
The company is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan aimed at cost-cutting and reconfiguring its delivery network.
JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ) shares rose more than 14% in premarket trading on Tuesday following the release of third-quarter results and guidance for 2027. The airline reported a loss per share of $0.60, compared to analyst estimates of $0.54. Revenue reached $2.81 billion, slightly below the $2.83 billion consensus estimate.
The airline posted an operating margin of negative 5.1% for the quarter. Operating revenue totaled $2.81 billion while operating expenses came in at $2.96 billion. The company's operating revenue increased 21% year-over-year.
Chief Executive Officer Joanna Geraghty said resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue ahead of initial expectations, allowing the company to offset more of the fuel cost increases than anticipated. She noted that Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver strong results even as the company grows capacity in that market.
Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma reports:
Coca-Cola ( KO ) posted better-than-expected third quarter results and raised its earnings outlook, but the company saw slowing demand in its North American business.
Coca-Cola stock traded lower in early trading.
The company posted adjusted earnings of $0.91 per share, above the $0.88 expected by Wall Street analysts, alongside revenue of $13.4 billion, also higher than estimates of $12.9 billion.
Overall unit case volume grew by 5%, more than the roughly 3% expected. The increase was once again led by Coke Zero, which grew roughly 16% year over year. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew by 6%.
Boeing ( BA ) shrank its quarterly losses and generated cash flow in the third quarter, but its top- and bottom-line results missed Wall Street's expectations.
Revenue of $24.1 billion and an adjusted loss per share of $0.34 came in below estimates of revenue of $24.3 billion and a loss of $0.20 per share.
The company's commercial airplane unit faced higher costs in its supply chain and for production as well as a $700 million charge on its 777X program. As a result, its operating margin in that segment fell to -6.5%.
"Backlog reached a record $745B. The 737-7 and 737-10 FAA certifications and F/A-XX award are meaningful milestones, though BCA margin deterioration to -6.5% from Q2's -2.7% introduces uncertainty around the recovery pace," CFRA analysts wrote in a note following the results.
SoFi ( SOFI ) stock surged 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the online financial services provider lifted its 2026 outlook and reported strong results for the third quarter.
Here's what SoFi reported for Q3, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 45.9% year over year to $1.39 billion, above estimates of $1.26 billion.
Adjusted earnings: $0.18, above estimates of $0.17.
Updated 2026 guidance: SoFi now expects net revenue of $5.04 billion in 2026, reflecting a 40% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected at $1.66 billion of adjusted EBITDA, and earnings per share are forecast at $0.61. Wall Street analysts were expecting 2026 earnings per share of $0.59.
The company also introduced 2027 guidance, guiding for $0.90 of earnings per share, which is above the Street's estimate of $ 0.82.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," CEO Anthony Noto said. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue."
Whirlpool posted another mixed quarter as inflation and lower demand in North America took a toll.
"What is new and different is the increasingly inflationary environment that has happened from Q2 into Q3, as well as the impact of volume deleveraging which is driven by the softer demand that we have in the North America industry," Whirlpool CFO Roxanne Warner told Yahoo Finance, adding that the team is focusing on what it can control.
In the third quarter, the company reported revenue declined by nearly 9% to $3.68 billion, which was below estimates of $3.91 billion. The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.21, lower than the adjusted earnings per share estimate of $0.76,  per Bloomberg consensus data
Warner said that the industry hasn't caught up to the "full impact of the inflationary pressures from 2022," with inflation up 12% since then.
For that reason,  the company plans to raise prices for the third time this year, now by 7% in the fourth quarter. That follows its largest price increase in history in April, at 10%, and a 4% increase in its list prices in July.
Revenue for major appliances in its North America business fell 8.3% year over year to $2.5 billion, below Wall Street's expectations.
Whirlpool's small domestic appliance business fell almost 1% to $286 million, below the expected $314 million. However, the company said that in the third quarter, some items sold out, leading to roughly 40% year-over-year growth in US orders in October.

What to know about the Iran war:
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in "perfect health," describing him as energetic, hopeful and composed following a meeting.
Khamenei was seriously wounded in the strikes that killed his father, Ali Khamenei, sources told CBS News in March. He has not been seen in public since the start of the war.
"The leader is in perfect health, and truly, what I observed during the meeting was a strong, energetic, hopeful and resolute spirit, along with inner peace," Ghalibaf said Tuesday.
"These qualities were fully evident in the leader," he added, "and I felt with all my being that this resolve and inner peace reflect a strong faith in Almighty God and a deep belief in the people."
The Saudi-led coalition fighting against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said Tuesday they had downed two ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, the Saudi capital.
"Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group toward the capital, Riyadh," spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki wrote in a post on X .
Multiple explosions were heard in Riyadh on Tuesday, journalists from the AFP news agency said.
Residents received a text-message alert on their mobile phones warning of an "aerial threat" and instructing them to seek shelter.
This latest attack follows weeks of strikes by the Houthis, who claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
A Kuwaiti State Security and Terrorism Criminal Court sentenced three men to death on Monday over an alleged plot to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef, with prosecutors accusing the defendants of spying for Iran, communicating with Iranian-linked entities and joining Hezbollah, two judicial sources told the AFP news agency Tuesday.
The court also sentenced eight other defendants to varying prison terms.
Those sentenced to death included cleric and National Islamic Alliance Secretary-General Hussein Abdullah Al-Maatouq and two other men. One of the defendants had previously been convicted of terrorism in 2016 and later received a pardon before being arrested again in April, the sources said.
According to Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Rai , the defendants were accused of communicating with Iran and entities allegedly operating in its interests, including Lebanese group Hezbollah, to carry out hostile acts against Kuwait following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on Feb. 28, at the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
The defendants were also accused of joining Hezbollah, a banned group in Kuwait, while knowing its objectives, and of engaging in activities allegedly intended to undermine the country's political, social and economic order and harm its national interests.
Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Qabas reported prosecutors accused the defendants of attempting to use explosives to carry out the alleged assassination plot and spread panic. One defendant was separately accused of attempting to bring explosives into the country to enable the others to carry out the alleged operation.
The reported Iran connection forms a central part of the case, although the allegations against the defendants do not, on their own, establish that the Iranian government directed the alleged assassination plot.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
"With the help of Almighty God, the Yemeni Armed Forces succeeded in targeting the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile," military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a post on X .
"The strike was accurate," he added, "and caused massive fires at the targeted site."
The alleged strike follows weeks of Houthi attacks against the world's top exporter of crude oil.
A resident in the nearby city of Al Khobar told the AFP news agency he heard explosions around dawn and then received a warning message on his phone.
"We got the alert on the mobile and then heard a very loud bang," the resident said.
The Ras Tanura facility along Saudi Arabia's eastern Gulf coast is home to one of the largest refineries in the Middle East and is a cornerstone of the kingdom's energy sector.
The complex has a capacity to refine 550,000 barrels per day. It has been repeatedly targeted by Iranian strikes, including a drone attack in early March that forced a partial shutdown of the refinery.
London — Two men have been charged with serious security offenses in Britain after being arrested in connection with the incident last month near RAF Fairford, the air base in England that had been used by the U.S. military to launch strikes on Iran, the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act.
Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."
The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England.
The U.S. embassy in Baghdad has shot down two drones, Saudi state television channel Al Arabya reported Tuesday.
An Iraqi security source told the outlet that air defenses protecting the embassy destroyed the drones.
The government-owned Iraqi television channel Al-Anbar reported that the head of Iraq's Security Media Cell, Saad Maan, said that explosions heard across the capital were the result of a drone being intercepted and shot down.
The drone's origin remains unknown, and no immediate reports of casualties or damage have been released. The U.S. State Department has not yet commented on the incident.
An oil slick in the Gulf has reached a beach in the United Arab Emirates, video from the AFP news agency showed on Tuesday, with experts warning it could threaten desalination plants as it spreads.
UAE authorities said Friday that they had "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches," referring to an emirate north of Dubai.
By Tuesday morning, footage shot by AFP showed workers cleaning up oil on the emirate's beaches, which had been shut earlier by authorities along with other beaches in the country.
Satellite images taken on Oct. 21 and analyzed by AFP show what appears to be a slick of about 70 square miles in that area. Three days later, images showed it had quadrupled in size to around 290 square miles.
Experts from NGOs including Dutch peace group PAX said oil came from the tanker GEM NO.2 after it was attacked on Oct. 9.
They warned the slick could affect operations at UAE desalination plants, crucial for supplying water to the Gulf country.
"Satellite imagery from October 26 shows oil slicks a few hundred metres away from the intake of the Naqaa desalination plant. It remains unclear to what extent this will affect the process at the plant itself,"  said Wim Zwijnenburg from PAX.
The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Oct. 9 that a vessel had been hit by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire that was later brought under control.

articles.content_orig:

On Monday, Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE: VZ ) CEO Dan Schulman sees opportunities to collaborate with satellite providers such as Elon Musk's Starlink , but says the wireless carrier has no reason to let Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) use its network to compete for mobile customers .
Speaking during Verizon's third-quarter earnings call, Schulman acknowledged that satellite connectivity could complement traditional wireless services, particularly in remote areas with limited cellular coverage.
"I do think there is a role for satellite for sure in remote areas. It's a great service for those customers," he said, adding, "And I do think there are ways that we can work together, either directly or through our JV with satellite providers, to provide a complementary service and a differentiated value proposition."
Schulman reiterated that the company has no plans to offer satellite providers access to its network through mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) agreements.
"I will say, and I'll repeat it again, that there are no backdoors to any of our MVNO agreements and I see absolutely no benefit whatsoever to extending an MVNO deal to any satellite provider," he added.
An MVNO, or mobile virtual network operator, sells wireless services using another carrier's network rather than relying entirely on its own infrastructure.
Read Also: Dow Surges Over 200 Points; Verizon Shares Fall Following Q3 Results
During the call, Schulman said Verizon takes SpaceX's ambitions seriously and assumes the company will execute its plans successfully.
He argued that competing directly with established wireless carriers would require SpaceX to build a substantial terrestrial network, including 65,000 to 80,000 macro sites, backhaul infrastructure, radio access equipment and significant spectrum resources.
Schulman estimated that such a buildout could take at least four to six years and cost $300 billion to $500 billion over seven to eight years.
He also dismissed the idea that Verizon must offer Starlink network access to prevent rivals from gaining an advantage.
"There is no benefit to Verizon Communications extending an MVNO deal," Schulman said, adding that the company intends to compete aggressively if SpaceX enters the market. "We will punch back hard when that happens," he said.
Verizon shares closed down 3.49% at $43.10 on Monday, despite the company reporting its strongest third-quarter wireless subscriber growth in five years, beating earnings expectations and raising its full-year outlook.
The stock gained 0.29% to $43.23 in after-hours trading, according to Benzinga Pro.
Verizon reported adjusted third-quarter earnings of $1.31 per share, topping analysts' expectations of $1.27 .
Revenue totaled $34.31 billion, missing the $34.74 billion consensus estimate as fewer customers upgraded their devices after handset subsidies were cut.

articles.title_orig: Apple Creator Studio gets powerful new AI features using OpenAI models
articles.title_zh: Apple Creator Studio gets powerful new AI features using OpenAI models
articles.content_orig:
Apple Creator Studio updates have today been announced, with what the company describes as “powerful new AI features” using a combination of Apple Intelligence and OpenAI models.
Final Cut Pro for Mac will also include built-in MotionVFX to provide a large collection of visual effects, transitions, and motion graphics tools …
Apple announced the updates alongside the new iMacs and 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip. It will be a free update for existing subscribers at some point in November.
Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX — an expansive collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, and motion graphics tools — as well as seamless editing in Pixelmator Pro. Apple’s curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro.
Music creators using Logic Pro for Mac gain a new intelligent assistant in beta, an enhanced Stem Splitter that now separates drums, and a redesigned Browser that incorporates all sounds, with music understanding and even a Splice library.
Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language.
Keynote, Pages, and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants 2 that understand document context and new Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for workflow automation. They also add stock video in the Content Hub and new premium themes and templates.
The headline news here is MotionVFX for Final Cut Pro.
Final Cut Pro for Mac now integrates MotionVFX directly into the app, giving editors access to thousands of elements, including templates with unique themes, stylish graphics, titles, and transitions, as well as tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Editors can also tap into the Content Hub directly within Final Cut Pro and access a library of Apple-curated stock videos, photos, and backgrounds to fill gaps, add polish, or spark new ideas without leaving their workflow.
Also notable is that the inclusion of OpenAI models alongside Apple Intelligence.
A new intelligent assistant powered by a combination of Apple-built models and OpenAI joins Logic Pro for Mac, helping creators and producers navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.
Visual productivity apps receive a new generation of intelligence features for subscribers, including an intelligent assistant, built on Apple models and OpenAI, directly within Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant understands document context to help users accomplish more without leaving their work.
In Keynote, the intelligent assistant helps with designing, animating, and refining slides. In Pages, it drafts, restructures, and fine-tunes written content. In Numbers, it calculates, visualizes, and organizes data; recommends suitable chart types with a one-tap preview; and builds custom tables using world knowledge.
New MCP support, built on this platform, enables external AI agents and tools to read content, perform edits, and execute automated actions directly in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers.
Apple hasn’t announced an exact launch date for the new features, instead saying that it will be “this November.”

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Issues Emergency Patch For Critical Google Algorithm Flaw
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Issues Emergency Patch For Critical Google Algorithm Flaw
articles.content_orig:
CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
On October 21, 2026, the Node.js Project published a security advisory for CVE-2026-111497 , an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js. The vulnerability affects the Node.js 26.x , 24.x , and 22.x release lines. Node.js rates the issue High, while Google, the CVE Numbering Authority (CNA), gives it a critical CVSSv4 score of 9.2 .
An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory. According to Node.js, this corruption can lead to a process crash, disclosure of sensitive process memory, or remote code execution. Exposure therefore depends on whether an application passes attacker-controlled compressed data to the affected decoder.
As of October 26, 2026, Rapid7 is not aware of exploitation in the wild, and CVE-2026-111497 is not listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog . However, given the vulnerability's potential to disclose memory or enable remote code execution (RCE), Rapid7 recommends that organizations prioritize remediation.
CVE-2026-111497 is classified as an out-of-bounds write ( CWE-787 ) and an unchecked return value ( CWE-252 ). Per the vendor advisory, the decoder handled an invalid Brotli block switch as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error. The streaming decoder then continued appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer, allowing malformed input to write beyond the buffer and corrupt process memory.
The vulnerability originates in Google Brotli, which the affected Node.js release lines bundle as a dependency. The CVE record identifies affected upstream Brotli ranges on all platforms as versions 1.0.3 before 1.0.10 , 1.1.0 before 1.1.1 , and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1 . The Node.js Project remediated its bundled decoder in the fixed Node.js releases listed below.
Because CVE-2026-111497 affects the upstream Google Brotli decoder, its reach is not limited to Node.js. Vendor and project advisories have also identified affected implementations in Bun , Python's Brotli and brotlicffi packages, .NET , Envoy and Istio , brotli4j , and operating-system packages . Affected versions, default exposure, and remediation vary by product; the presence of an affected decoder does not by itself establish exposure unless an application processes attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should consult the relevant downstream vendor or distribution advisories to identify affected versions, assess exposure, and determine appropriate remediation.
Vendor-supplied security updates are available to remediate CVE-2026-111497. Organizations running an affected Node.js release should upgrade on an urgent basis, outside of normal patch cycles:
Node.js 22.x releases before 22.23.4 are affected; upgrade to 22.23.4 or later.
Node.js 24.x releases before 24.22.1 are affected; upgrade to 24.22.1 or later.
Node.js 26.x releases before 26.12.1 are affected; upgrade to 26.12.1 or later.
The vendor states that end-of-life Node.js release lines should also be treated as affected when a security release occurs. Organizations using an end-of-life release should migrate to a supported, fixed release line. Node.js has not published a vendor-supported workaround; if an immediate upgrade is not possible, Rapid7 recommends restricting or disabling application paths that decompress untrusted Brotli data as a temporary exposure-reduction measure.
For the latest mitigation guidance, please refer to the Node.js security advisory .
Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-111497 with an authenticated Linux and macOS vulnerability check expected to be available in the October 26 content release. Windows-based vulnerability check is in progress and an update will be provided soon. Please refer to this blog for the latest information.

Ed Nightingale, vice president of Digital Products at General Motors, spoke to FOX Business about the OnStar AI Assistant, data privacy and safety.
General Motors announced Tuesday that it will transfer its stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq next month, a move the Detroit automaker said reflects its growing focus on technology and innovation.
The company said its shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov. 17 under the existing ticker symbol "GM."
"GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM Chief Financial Officer Paul Jacobson said in a statement. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy."
GM, which operates the Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac brands, has increasingly emphasized advanced vehicle technology as a key part of its long-term growth strategy.
GM EXPANDS ‘EYES-OFF’ AUTONOMOUS DRIVING PLANS TO PICKUPS AND SUVS
President of General Motors Marc Reuss delivers a speech during the brand's annual technology event in New York on Oct. 21, 2026. (Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images)
The listing change comes as GM continues investing in technologies aimed at making vehicles safer, smarter and more efficient, while expanding its electric vehicle offerings.
The transfer could make GM eligible for inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index, which tracks 100 of the largest non-financial companies listed on the exchange, but inclusion is not guaranteed.
GM LETTING SOME EV OWNERS SELL ELECTRICITY BACK TO THE US POWER GRID
The General Motors world headquarters at Detroit's Renaissance Center. (Paul Hennessy/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
GM shares will remain listed on the NYSE through the close of trading on Nov. 16.
The automaker said existing shareholders will not need to take any action as a result of the transfer.

LONDON, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Oil futures fell on Tuesday as attention turned to Middle East peace talks, though prices remain near multi-month highs as the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict rages and the potential for fresh US-Israeli attacks hangs over the market.
Brent crude futures were down $1.00, or 0.86%, at $114.81 a barrel by 1311 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 78 cents, or 0.77%, at $100.98.
Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday met Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei a day after holding talks with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.
State media said Khamenei had emphasised the importance of pursuing Iran's interests and maintaining its conditions for ending the war.
The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media said.
Scope for peace has been dented, however, by renewed attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on key oil producer Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said on Tuesday that they had struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the ⁠biggest in the kingdom, with a ballistic missile.
October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.
Swiss bank UBS said it expects Brent prices to stay elevated near $110 a barrel through to the end of the year, citing volatile Middle East supply and geopolitical uncertainty. It was previously forecasting $100 a barrel at the end of this year.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has risen but the number of vessel attacks has increased, with risks likely to become more acute if US naval support wavers, UBS said.
Brent prices surged to more than $117 a barrel last week for their highest since April, buoyed by a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent touched $117 on Monday as well.
"The impression now is that there is a significant risk premium in crude oil prices for the risk that the US/Israel will attack Iran in the coming weeks," said SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop.
Investors were also looking for cues from a general election in Israel on Tuesday.
"The outcome of today’s parliamentary elections in Israel could also be significant for further developments in the war with Iran, as Israeli Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu, if re-elected, might attempt to achieve regime change in Iran," Commerzbank analysts wrote.
(Reporting by Robert Harvey in London and Anjana Anil in BengaluruEditing by Joe Bavier and David Goodman)

articles.title_orig: Apple updates the MacBook Pro with M6 chips
articles.title_zh: Apple updates the MacBook Pro with M6 chips
articles.content_orig:
The entry-level MacBook Pro gets Apple’s latest silicon including its N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
The entry-level MacBook Pro gets Apple’s latest silicon including its N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
Apple is giving its entry-level MacBook Pro a spec bump. After upgrading the entry-level MacBook Pro with its M5 chip a year ago, Apple is refreshing the laptop today with the M6 chip, which the company launched in August as part of recent upgrades to the new Mac Mini.
Last year’s entry-level MacBook Pro update brought minimal changes from the M4 model that debuted a year prior, including the same design, port layout, webcam, and speakers. The most notable updates, aside from the then-new M5 processor, was faster storage and the option to upgrade its capacity to a hefty 4TB for an extra $1,200.
It’s a similar story for 2026. Announced this morning through a press release , the new 14-inch MacBook Pro features three Thunder 4 USB-C ports that all support charging and DisplayPort connectivity, a MagSafe 3 charging port, full-size HDMI, and an SDXC memory card slot accommodating photographers. It carries forward the same 12MP Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, but this year the 14-inch MacBook Pro is getting an upgrade to both Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 through the Apple N1 wireless networking chip that was previously only included on MacBook Pro configurations with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Pricing for the new M6 version of the 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 with 16GB of memory, the same as last year’s M5 model. Bumping that to 24GB increases the price to $2,199, while 32GB is $2,399. Included storage starts at 1TB, but increasing that is now more expensive as a result of the current memory shortage . Bumping that to 2TB is an extra $500, while 4TB is now an extra $1,500. Preorders start on October 28th and shipping is expected to begin on November 6th.
The new M6 processor is Apple’s first 2nm chip with a bump to a 12-core CPU, up from 10 cores in the M5, and the company says it offers up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance when compared to its predecessor. The M6 also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine to handle heavy on-device AI tasks, plus an upgraded 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core. In addition to performance improvements, Apple says its M6 processor is more power efficient.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO Filing Calms Nerves With Signs of Healthy Growth
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO Filing Calms Nerves With Signs of Healthy Growth
articles.content_orig:
When Anthropic goes public, the stock its seven cofounders hold stands to be worth up to $200 billion between them, carved up into seven nearly identical piles.
Each cofounder, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, holds a stake of between 231 million and 244 million shares. Those stakes would be worth about $21 billion to $30 billion apiece, if Anthropic’s IPO values the company at $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, as some some media reports have indicated the company hopes to do.
The founders’ equity includes exactly 2,185,400 stock options that each person can cash in now and 639,500 restricted stock units that vest after the IPO. Based on Fortune’s analysis, the share ownership gives each cofounder between 1.4% and 1.5% of the company and all told, the debut offering will amp the group’s wealth on paper to about $200 billion. (Full caveat, Anthropic hasn’t priced its shares and the exact details are subject to change. Fortune laid out the math in earlier analyses .)
The approach completely flattens the idea of the pyramid-shaped pay structure you find at most mega-cap public companies with a CEO or founder at the top making the most in cash and equity. At Anthropic, the core septet has no apparent pay pyramid, despite Dario Amodei serving as CEO alongside Daniela Amodei as president and board chairperson. The seven appear to hold nearly identical stakes, and each gets one vote in the entity that will control the company’s shareholder vote, with a separate trust set up to elect the majority of the board.
Robin Ferracone, founder of compensation consulting firm Farient Advisors, said the “egalitarian approach” Anthropic took with its founder group is unusual and noted that seven founders is a “relatively large” group. “It’s unusual to give all the founders the same thing,” said Ferracone. It usually evolves eventually as awards start to vest and pay becomes more linked to positions.
Anthropic described the group “distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission,” in the registration statement filed Monday, although it singles out Dario and Daniela as “critical to setting our strategic direction,” and says they would be “difficult to replace.”
There also appears to be no sibling rivalry here, at least not yet. The Amodeis as cofounders take equal pay, including annual increases to cash or equity. Last year, both brother and sister took home $654,167 in salary, plus stock and options the filing values at about $13 million combined that would be worth about $330 million at a $2 trillion valuation. They got raises in July, and now both are taking home $1.4 million in salary. In February, Anthropic gave each about 1.4 million stock options and 2.4 million more RSUs, and another 537,000 RSUs in July. The RSUs start paying out once Anthropic goes public in quarterly installments over the next several years, as long  as the Amodeis are still at the company.  At a $2 trillion valuation, the grants are worth about $505 million each.
“We take internal parity into account when determining executive compensation,” Anthropic’s newly filed registration statement explains. “Each co-founder is paid equal compensation.”
Anthropic’s filing only shows pay for the Amodeis since they are the only two cofounders Anthropic counts as executive officers. The other five in the initial seven—Tom Brown, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Jack Clark, and Chris Olah, hold C-level titles such as chief compute officer and chief science officer, but don’t appear in the company’s pay tables. However, all seven hold identical numbers of options and RSUs that will vest by late November. They align, within a few shares, of the disclosed grants to the Amodeis, which implies the other five got the same awards.
The approach is worlds away from SpaceX, the last company to go public at this scale. In the months before its June 2026 IPO , SpaceX gave Musk a total of 1.3 billion restricted shares in two awards. Both are tied to market-value milestones with one attached to the creation of a human colony on Mars and data centers in space for the other. If he achieves the plan goals including the Mars colony, the awards could be worth $650 billion to $700 billion. No one else at SpaceX comes close.
And unlike Musk’s SpaceX awards, each Anthropic founder has pledged to give 80% of their stock to philanthropy, which could amount to an $80 billion to $165 billion total gift, although the pledges aren’t legally binding. The founders’ awards are structured such that they can maintain control over Anthropic even if they donate away their wealth. Musk, in a post on X last week, pledged to give every child in America a share of his SpaceX stock.
The founders can’t sell stock right away, although all seven are listed as selling stockholders in the IPO. Under the IPO’s lockup terms, the magnificent seven can start selling a portion of their stock about six months after the offering and the rest after about a year. Some have already started to cash in. The Amodeis sold shares in a tender offer in April at $25.91 a share, according to the S-1.
The two board members who will oversee executive comp at Anthropic following the IPO are both investors in the AI frontier lab. Vas Narasimhan, the CEO of Novartis , chairs Anthropic’s compensation committee. Narasimhan bought about $10 million worth of stock in May through a company he owns with his wife a few weeks after joining Anthropic’s board. The comp committee’s other member, Yasmin Razavi, is a general partner at Spark Capital, whose funds have invested $777 million in Anthropic since 2023.
Amanda Gerut is the west coast editor at Fortune , overseeing publicly traded businesses, executive compensation, Securities and Exchange Commission regulations, and investigations.
