articles.title_orig: Ford’s sub-$30K electric truck puts the home backup inverter right inside the vehicle
articles.title_zh: Ford’s sub-$30K electric truck puts the home backup inverter right inside the vehicle
articles.content_orig:
Ford’s upcoming electric truck integrates an onboard inverter to dramatically slash the cost, hardware, and utility red tape of home backup power.
Ford’s upcoming electric truck integrates an onboard inverter to dramatically slash the cost, hardware, and utility red tape of home backup power.
We’re still a few months away from the official reveal of the Ford Fathom , the automaker’s first next-generation electric vehicle. While we wait, Ford has been whetting our appetite with news about the sub-$30,000 pickup — including today’s announcement about the Fathom’s bidirectional charging capabilities.
With an increasing number of EVs coming out with bidirectional vehicle-to-home (V2H) or vehicle-to-load (V2L) charging capabilities, Ford is trying to position the Fathom as a key entrant — and one that simplifies the system by making it an everyday reality rather than a $10,000 luxury perk. Unlike the discontinued F-150 Lightning, which required a massive, expensive external DC-to-AC wall inverter, the Fathom packs the inverter directly into its onboard “E-box” to pump out over 10 kW of AC power natively.
The Fathom’s built-in inverter converts its battery power into standard household electricity to run appliances, back up a home during an outage, or feed energy back into the grid.
Taking advantage of these features will require additional hardware, though Ford aims to make it significantly cheaper than current options. To send power back to the grid, owners will need the Ford Home Power Station. Ford is targeting a 50 percent discount compared to the existing $1,310 Ford Charge Station Pro. For whole-home backup power during a blackout, owners must pair that station with a backup panel. While that combination typically runs around $5,205, Ford is aiming for an estimated $3,123 — a roughly 40 percent reduction — though finalized pricing for both packages is still pending.
The Fathom, a $28,000 electric pickup truck, will be the first vehicle on Ford’s new Universal Electric Vehicle Platform , an innovative new system designed to maximize aerodynamic range while also reducing production costs so Ford can make a profitable EV. For over a year, the company has been hyping it as its “Model T moment” that will revolutionize nearly everything at the 123-year-old company.
Another barrier to V2H or V2L charging is red tape from public utilities. Ford’s solution was to team up with five of North America’s biggest power companies — Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E); American Electric Power (AEP); BC Hydro; Consumers Energy; and Exelon — which collectively cover millions of customers in the US and Canada. Ford theorized that whatever rules they agree on will likely become the standard everyone else follows. They agreed to cut the paperwork for basic storm backup, use common plugs and software, and make grid programs automatic.
Cutting the cost of the Ford Home Power Station and Backup Panel is certainly helpful, but homeowners will still face additional costs related to permitting, electrician labor, and heavy-gauge wiring. These could conspire to keep these bidirectional charging features out of reach for some customers.
Still, Ford is intent on keeping the costs low for its new electric truck. With supply chain constraints and trade upheaval, that will remain a central challenge for the automaker as it gets closer to one of the most important vehicle debuts in Ford’s history.

articles.content_orig:

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. And by that, he doesn’t just mean assembly, but the production of every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today.
Anduril is partnering with Qualcomm to achieve that mission with a new computer called BlueChip, the companies announced Tuesday. BlueChip will be available for preorder in 2027.
While technical details are scant — Anduril hasn’t even finished contracting with all its component suppliers yet, according to Luckey — this first product will be a hardened laptop. It will be designed to withstand the most grueling physical environments and meet the security-conscious needs of the military, government, first responders and law enforcement.
For the first generation, about 90% of its components will be made in the U.S. or in allied countries, Anduril says, most notably its CPU. BlueChip will run on a Snapdragon X Series built at TSCM’s massive new facility in Arizona. The CPU uses the same architecture that powers other laptops, including the Microsoft Surface, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said during the press conference.
“As of right now, the laptop’s bill of materials is about 90% U.S. and allied [ally countries], and we have a technical roadmap to get to 100% domestic over time,” Luckey said. “The intent in the long run is to have an option that is made entirely in the United States, 100% domestic. And I mean everything. I mean the displays. I mean the metallics. I mean the the magnetics. All of it.”
Right now, for instance, Luckey says he’s found an American supplier for the glass that covers the display, but the display itself is one of several components he says are only manufactured in China.
While Luckey says consumers are welcome to order a BlueChip — the company may even create a waiting list for interested consumers — this first PC won’t be designed for them. For one thing, as a hardened computer, it will be heavy and have battery-life constraints because of the engineering required to  withstand rain, dust, and other rugged conditions.
The bigger point is to offer U.S. government agencies a product that complies with regulations requiring them to buy U.S.-made computers. In this case, the selling point is a transparent supply chain that customers can track and audit.
“These computers are the anti-surveillance computer. You fully control it,” Luckey described in a recent interview. “You know everything that is in it, every single component, and you know every software component that is running on it.”
Anduril is also working to ensure that the Arm-based machine works well with Windows apps, apps built for certain Linux distributions used by the government, and even archaic software that various agencies still run.
While Anduril hasn’t yet announced pricing, Luckey estimates it will cost about 20% more than typical high-end PCs.
“As much as I love BlueChip, if I was just a normal consumer making a rational decision without a kind of patriotic basis, I’d be better off buying a Dell laptop than an Anduril laptop because it’s going to be cheaper. I’m just talking about your average person consumer, right, who doesn’t have any real need for this,” Luckey said.
But Luckey clearly hopes Anduril will eventually make U.S.-made laptops more in line with consumer desires. He said the product is the first in what he envisions as a full line of BlueChip computers, noting that he began his career making devices virtual reality headsets for consumers.
“I’m buying American cars, and then I buy a computer that’s made on the other side of the world, not just China, but you know, Japan, Korea,” he said. “It’s kind of humiliating that as an American and my birthright is computers, in my opinion, because America invented them, that I’m not able to buy an American computer.”
As for the potentially expensive folly of trying to take on China’s electronics components manufacturing industry single-handedly, Luckey joked about his internal reputation for “being a nut” with such big ideas. (He admits that he pushed his board to spend $900 million to build a factory for a jet before the company had even won a contract.)
“This is not one of those things. My investors do not think I’m a crazy person in this particular area,” he said. In fact, rugged computers are already about a $5 billion market .

Browser maker Opera has introduced a new web standard that lets users to run AI models directly in its browser, without relying on the cloud.
The new standard, WebAI, is designed to work with a variety of AI models. Opera name drops Google’s Gemma — an open-weight model that Google first introduced two years ago — as one example. On Macs, WebAI also supports Apple’s on-device foundation model, the company says.
But Opera says WebAI isn’t tied to any particular model and is built to support a wide range of open-weight AI systems. WebAI grew out of previous work by Opera to bring locally run models into its browsers.
Opera is making the new AI features available as an early preview in its flagship Opera One browser. The company says Opera GX, its browser built for gamers and streamers, and Opera Neon, its browser that uses AI agents to perform tasks, will soon get the same treatment. Users have to choose to opt into the feature, according to the company.
Open-weight models offer a number of benefits to users. For one, they are typically free to download and use. Their underlying model weights are also publicly available, which gives developers more freedom to customize how they work. Although unlike fully open-source software, open-weight models still come with some restrictions.
There’s the additional advantage of privacy, the company said. Users can tap into AI features without having to send their personal information to a company’s servers or pay for a cloud-based AI subscription.
“Developers can add AI features without running AI infrastructure or paying for every request,” the company said in its announcement. “Users don’t need AI subscriptions, the information the local AI handles stays on their own device, and they stay in control of the AI on their computer.”
The company said WebAI also allows anyone to generate text, classify content, and understand how pieces of information relate, all directly in the browser.
Privacy has become a growing concern as AI assistants become more powerful and gain access to personal information. Users often surrender vast amounts of personal information with AI chatbots, sometimes without a clear understanding of how that data is stored or used.
Locally run models offer an alternative because the processing happens on the user’s own device — and not on a company’s cloud server. That doesn’t eliminate every privacy risk, but it does give users a bit more control. It makes sense then that Opera has made digital privacy one of its primary selling points over the years.
There are trade-offs, however. Running AI models locally puts more demand on a user’s computer, which can affect performance. Opera notes that model performance will depend on the  device’s hardware.

articles.title_orig: Why Netflix stock just can't catch a break after earnings
articles.title_zh: Why Netflix stock just can't catch a break after earnings
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The dreadful year for Netflix ( NFLX ) investors just keeps getting more dreadful.
A fresh sell-off on the day after a lackluster earnings report on Oct. 20 has persisted, with Netflix shares down about 7% in the past five trading sessions. The S&P 500 is relatively flat during this stretch.
Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace analysis shows Netflix shares trading at one of the lowest trailing 12-month P/E ratios in the past decade.
Netflix stock is down 32% year to date.
If price is truth in the stock market, then Netflix's slide reflects its truths. They include lost viewership to rival YouTube, a less-than-hot content slate this year, and a view on Wall Street that content spending will have to increase dramatically in 2027 to regain eyeballs.
The third quarter for Netflix reflected all of this and then some.
Netflix delivered a mixed third quarter earnings report, with earnings of $0.87 per share, beating Wall Street estimates of $0.82. Revenue of $12.87 billion came in line with analysts' expectations.
For the fourth quarter, Netflix forecast revenue of $13.44 billion, below then expectations of $13.57 billion. The company also cut its full-year advertising revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion previously.
"The US is also working," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told analysts on an earnings call. "It's just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like. We had some really solid doubles and triples this year. But the other territories count on some of those titles being home runs so that they'll travel around the world."
To reboot the bull case for the stock, Sarandos pushed the button on laying off 6% of the workforce. He sent well-regarded chief content officer Bela Bajaria packing in favor of former Disney ( DIS ) exec Peter Rice.
"2026 has been more of a transitional year than we envisioned. While the latest Ads miss is frustrating, we find comfort in Membership retention that is still healthy and corrective actions within content that can drive a potential re-acceleration in 2027E and into 2028E (which we are not modeling today)," KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson said.

With less than two weeks to go until his Apostolic Journey to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, Pope Leo XIV has renewed his âgreat joy and enthusiasmâ to undertake this journey on November 6-17.
A statement released on Monday by the Holy See Press Office confirmed that the journey will take place according to the previously-released schedule.
It said the Popeâs journey will âoffer opportunities to strengthen the bonds of communion with the local Churches, encourage the faithful in their mission, and bring a message of faith, hope, and peace to the peoples of Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, encountering the faith of their peoples, and sharing with them the hope and peace that Christ brings to our world.â
Pope Leo expressed his hopes that the visit to Latin America will strength Christians' commitment to proclaiming the Gospel.
âI am looking forward to returning to the continent where Iâve experienced so many moments of my life,â said the Pope in the statement. âMay this journey be an occasion for us to open our hearts to one another, strengthen our communion as brothers and sisters, and renew our commitment to proclaiming the Gospel with joy.â
Regarding the Popeâs recovery from surgery on October 13, the statement said the Holy Fatherâs recovery âcontinues to progress, in accordance with the favorable assessments communicated by his medical team.â
âAs previously reported, the surgical procedure was successful and without complications. Subsequent medical examinations confirmed that the condition was localized and that no further oncological treatment is necessary,â it added.
The statement noted that Pope Leo has gradually resumed his activities while adjusting his daily schedule in consultation with his doctors âto prioritize his recovery while continuing to fulfill the responsibilities of his ministry.â
âHe has maintained important appointments and public engagements, remaining attentive to the needs of each day and allowing for appropriate periods of rest,â it said.
The Pope remains âdeeply grateful for the prayers and affection he has received from throughout the world and for the dedicated care of the medical professionals who have accompanied him during his recovery.â
The Holy See Press Office statement went on to refer Dr. Luigi Carboneâs words on the Popeâs recovery.
âDr. Luigi Carbone confirms that the Holy Fatherâs recovery after the surgery continues, and the latest medical examinations attest to his good health and favorable clinical condition,â it said. âBased on his current clinical status, as well as the instrumental and laboratory tests performed, there are no contraindications that would prevent him from undertaking his upcoming Apostolic Journey to Latin America as planned. The Pope is following medical recommendations with great care and diligence, and with a deep determination to continue serving the Church.â

articles.title_orig: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.title_zh: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.content_orig:
Just one child doomed China’s hopes of overtaking the US.
The Middle Kingdom, once a surging economic growth engine expected to eclipse the US economy in just a few years, is not expected to outgrow the US until the 2040s now — if it does at all.
And it’s largely down to China’s 1979 One Child Policy , which is devastating growth, according to Yi Fuxian, a Chinese demographer at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Plummeting birth rates and economic problems have erased the 6+% per year growth that China reported before the COVID-19 pandemic.
Many economists in both China and the West were taken in by the Chinese Communist Party’s inflated official figures, which massively overestimated the country’s consumer power, Fuxian said.
It comes as a Goldman Sachs study found that China’s population began shrinking in 2022 , just 13 years after that of neighboring Japan. And its decline is on track to be far steeper, dramatically damaging the country’s economic prospects, the Financial Times reported .
China has a GDP of $21.6 trillion — just two-thirds the size of the US economy.
Yi told The Post that official Chinese statistics have systematically inflated the country’s birthrates and total population figures going back decades.
While official reports claim China has a population of over 1.4 billion, Yi calculates that the true figure in 2020 was “under 1.28 billion,” at least 130 million lower than reported.
India actually surpassed China as the world’s most populous nation years earlier than officially recognized, according to Yi, author of the 2007 book, “Big Country with an Empty Nest,” which criticized China’s one-child policies.
The US, the third most populous country in the world, has 342 million people — about a quarter the population of China.
Yi argues that China’s population actually began shrinking in 2018, four years earlier than Goldman Sachs’ estimate, and more than a decade before the official projection of 2031 to 2034.
Most of this can be attributed to China’s notorious One Child Policy , instituted to limit Chinese families to one child per mother, over fears of spiraling population growth and widespread poverty.
While the policy was relaxed to two children per couple in 2016 and three children in 2021, China’s total fertility rate remains one of the lowest in the world .
China is no longer poor — officially 0% of the population is in extreme poverty, compared to 88% 40 years ago.
But it’s also not rich; the per capita GDP is about $13,800 per year, about 15% of that in the US.
Turkey, Russia and Kazakhstan are all richer than China by that measure.
The country’s total fertility rate fell below the 2.1 replacement level in 1991 and continued to plummet, dropping below 1.0 and now estimated to be just 0.8 births per woman, according to Yi.
Last year saw a record low of just 8 million live births in China. The much smaller US, by contrast, had 3.6 million births.
Yi also blames the economic reforms of China’s former Premier Zhu Rongji in the 1990s, for causing “many problems” that slowed down China’s economic growth and race to catch up with the US.
Decades of strict birth restrictions and fiscal centralization severely curtailed household disposable income in China, to roughly 42-44% of GDP.
In contrast, in the US, that figure is over 70% of GDP.
While this may have helped China’s economy in the short term, allowing it to flood the US with cheap imported goods, in the long run, it may have signed the CCP’s suicide note, according to Yi.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
Children function as “super-consumers,” driving much of household spending, he explained.
With China missing several full generations worth of children, this severely crippled Chinese domestic consumption, he argued.
To offset weak domestic consumption, China became heavily dependent on manufacturing exports, an unsustainable real estate bubble, and state-subsidized industrial overcapacity, he explained.
Those policies, “killed China’s economy, the population and the economy — and also killed America’s manufacturing,” Yi said.
China is now one of the oldest countries in the world, with a rapidly shrinking labor pool and aging population. The median age is expected to reach 59 by 2050, compared to 44 in the US.
This means Beijing may never catch up with the US economically — and worse, could face a long-term economic deceleration, Yi argued.
Yi puts the over-optimistic predictions about China’s economic growth down to mainstream economists and Chinese government-aligned institutions relying on fabricated data — assuming China’s population would soon grow five times larger than the US.
This played into the popular narrative that “the East is rising while the West is declining,” he said, while the truth is very different.
“By 2029 to 2035, China will lag behind the US across all major demographic and growth metrics,” Yi said.
However, for pro-democracy activists who might hope that this demographic time bomb could topple the CCP, Yi has a warning.
Contrary to Western expectations that economic development would foster a pro-democracy middle class, China’s rapid aging has depleted it of the young population required to drive political activism.
Just 16% of China is aged 15 to 29, down from 31% at the time of China’s last mass-democracy movement in 1989, which culminated in the communists’ brutal crackdown in Tiananmen Square.
An aging, risk-averse China is far more likely to support a centralized strongman who will safeguard pensions and social stability, Yi explained.

articles.content_orig:

Digital financial services company SoFi Technologies ( SOFI ) announced better-than-expected revenue in Q3 2026, with revenue up 45.9% year on year to $1.39 billion. The company's full-year revenue guidance of $6.4 billion at the midpoint came in 31.1% above analysts' consensus estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.18 per share was 7.4% above analysts' consensus estimates.
For more on SoFi, read our full research report .

Revenue $1.39 billion vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $1.26 billion (45.9% year-on-year growth, 9.6% beat)
Pre-tax profit $317.8 million (22.9% margin)
Adjusted EPS $0.18 vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $0.17 (7.4% beat)
Market capitalization $18.68 billion
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," said Anthony Noto, CEO of SoFi. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue. Our conviction in the opportunity ahead has never been greater."
A company's long-term performance is an indicator of its overall quality. Any business can put up a good quarter or two, but the best consistently grow over the long haul. SoFi's 38.7% annualized revenue growth over the last five years was strong. Its growth surpassed the average financials company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.
Long-term growth matters most, but within financials, a half-decade historical view may miss recent interest rate changes, market returns and industry trends. SoFi's annualized revenue growth of 38.1% over the last two years aligns with its five-year trend, suggesting demand remained predictably strong.
This quarter, SoFi reported year-on-year revenue growth of 45.9%, and its $1.39 billion of revenue beat Wall Street's consensus estimates by 9.6%.
Transaction volume and loan originations represent the core activity metrics that drive revenue growth across the financial services landscape. This overall volume serves as the primary engine of a firm's top-line performance.
SoFi's volumes have grown at an annual rate of 37.3% over the last five years, much faster than the broader financials industry but slower than its total revenue. Over the last two years, volume growth accelerated to 63.4% annually. Its recent performance could signal a better outlook.
SoFi's volumes totaled $16.9 billion this quarter, beating analysts' consensus estimates by 17.4%. That was 70.3% higher than the same quarter last year.
SoFi delivered a solid quarter, with revenue beating analysts' consensus estimates by a wide margin and full-year revenue guidance also topping Wall Street's consensus. Those were key positives in the report. Shares surged 8.5% to $15.70 immediately after the release.
SoFi reported solid earnings, but one quarter doesn't necessarily make the stock a buy. When making that decision, it's important to consider its valuation and business quality, as well as what has happened in the latest quarter. For more on SoFi, read our full research report here (it's free) .

It’s time to start making your holiday gift list. And that can be a lot of pressure when there’s a lot to choose from. Some tech isn’t worth what it costs, while others are underrated and changing our day-to-day — like our favorite three-in-one portable fan or easy-to-use coffee maker with biodegradable pods.
Our CNET editors handpicked 15 tech gifts to help you feel more confident in your choice before it arrives. Whether you’re looking for a screen-free tech gift for your kid or the easy-to-use home tech gift that makes the day-to-day a little easier, there’s a gift for everyone at every price point to make checking off your wish list a little easier.
It’s been 13 years since the next chapter of Grand Theft Auto was released, but it’s finally coming. And it’s the one gamers are bound to be talking about. Grand Theft Auto 6 continues with characters Jason and Lucia as they take on missions in Leonida. In usual GTA fashion, we can expect nods to popular films and figures, as we have in earlier GTA games.
GTA 6 marks the first original game from the popular video game publisher, Rockstar, since Red Dead Redemption 2 was released in 2018 — not including remasters of other games. GTA 6 will be the latest game from Rockstar since then.
GTA 6 will be released on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X and Series S . However, preorders are available now on Rockstar, but if you preorder before Nov. 20, you’ll get the Vintage Vice City Pack for free. Physical copies of GTA 6 are not expected to be available at launch.
If you want a friendlier or more relaxing Pokemon game instead of the typical pocket monster battles, Pokemon Pokopia is it. In this video game, you’ll play the character Ditto and help the Pokemon by joining forces to rebuild their world after all humans have vanished. The game’s style resembles Animal Crossing and could be your new evening escape. However, Pokemon Pokopia is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2 .
If you’re looking for another Pokemon tech gadget, keep scrolling. It’s already on my holiday shopping list for my kid.
Of all of Apple’s AirPods models, the latest AirPods 5 is the one to buy if you’re in the market for new earbuds . Both the base and step-up models of the AirPods 5 have some upgrades from the AirPods 4 . Both versions have active noise cancellation and improved sound. However, the step-up model costs $149 and has a wireless charging case and an extra hour of battery life — even with ANC enabled.
The Bruvi Pod Coffee Maker is an aesthetically pleasing smart coffee maker that has all the features to fulfill your dreams of a barista-level cup of joe from home. You can make espresso, cold brew, iced and drip coffee. Our kitchen experts say it makes pretty good crema for your espresso shots, too. Bruvi’s machine walks you through each step with an easy-to-navigate touchscreen and symbols. And the B-Pods are biodegradable, so you can worry less about polluting the environment with your single-serve B-Pods because they’re designed to break down in the landfill.
If you’re looking for another coffee maker option without worrying about pods, Caraway’s  plastic-free coffee maker may be an environmentalist’s dreams, too. It has a Clean Brew System that’s made of stainless steel and glass.
The Caraway Coffee Maker has a glass water reservoir, stainless steel water path and a stainless steel shower head to evenly distribute hot water across your coffee grounds. It also has a stainless steel brew basket and a glass carafe. Plus, you’ll get a stainless steel coffee ground scoop and a stainless steel reusable coffee filter.
You can quietly brew and descale your coffee with a dial control. And it has a 90-minute warming feature to keep your coffee warm when it’s finished brewing. Caraway’s coffee machine comes in four colors and is backed by a two-year limited warranty.
Best lightweight budget MacBook
If you’re leaning toward giving your kid a new laptop or want a new one for casual online shopping, the MacBook Neo could be a good choice. The MacBook Neo is Apple’s budget-friendly laptop that has the look and feel of its premium laptop, the MacBook Pro . But it starts at a much lower price point of $689. It’s durable, lightweight and has a slightly bigger display than the MacBook Air . The MacBook Neo also has USB-C charging and uses the A18 power chip just like the iPhone 16 Pro .
Touch ID is available on the Neo’s upgraded model and 512GB of storage, which costs $100 more.
Shark’s StainForce is a battery-powered cordless handheld vacuum that feels like a must-have if you have pets. It works on multiple surfaces, including carpet, hardwood and upholstery like couches. Plus, we like that Shark’s StainForce is lightweight, making it ideal for quickly cleaning up small messes. Plus, the suction is powerful enough to clean up new spills, old couch stains, pet hair and even cat puke — a mess our editor tried cleaning himself.
The Shark Stainforce includes a stain removal spray that can be kept in the vacuum’s side caddy and there’s a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner to tackle tight spots.
The Google Pixel 10A is CNET’s best budget-friendly phone, costing $499. If you were considering the Pixel 9A , note that the 10A offers upgrades that make it our top pick. There’s an upgraded camera with a flat rear camera flush with the phone. You can expect other features, like built-in Gemini and wireless charging. And the battery has 5,100-mAh capacity, which gives over 30 hours of battery life.
Plus, Google promises that you’ll get seven years of software and security updates before you need to upgrade to a new smartphone. And if you’re upgrading from an iPhone, you can send files and photos to an iPhone through AirDrop .
The iPhone 16 isn’t Apple’s latest smartphone, but it’s still one of CNET’s best smartphones . It has a few of the same hardware features as the new iPhone 18 Pro , like the side Camera Control and Action buttons. We like that it still has great picture quality and it’s equipped with Apple Intelligence . Plus, many of Apple’s smartphone updates come in the software upgrades, so you’ll get everything iOS 27 has to offer — including Siri AI when it’s out of beta testing. Best of all, since the iPhone 16 starts at $799 for 128GB of storage, you’ll get all these features for a fraction of the price of Apple’s new premium models, which start at $1,200.
Best magnetic power bank overall
Iniu’s wireless charger is MagSafe, so you can snap it on the back of your smartphone to charge on the go. This one’s a pretty slim portable charger compared to other options. It has two USB-C ports and comes with a wired charging cable to charge your phone or the charger, but heads up: It includes a short cord.
Iniu says it charges quickly, taking the iPhone 17 Pro from 0% to 50% in 33 minutes and from 20% to 78% in 25 minutes. And the charger has an LED display showing how much battery life it has left. However, Iniu’s SnapGo Air charger only works with iPhone 12-18 models.
The iRobot Roomba 205 is a robot vacuum that can map out your home and clean your floors smoothly — even in the dark. The combo has a built-in DustCompactor that compacts dirt in the robot. And Roomba says you can clean for up to 60 days without needing to empty it, plus it doesn’t require a dock.
We like that it can clean different surfaces and has a three-stage cleaning process. You can choose the suction level, schedule cleanings, choose rooms to clean up a mess, skip or give a few extra cleaning passes for heavy traffic areas. The price will depend on which model you choose. The iRobot Roomba 205 DustCompactor is originally priced at $450, while the vacuum and mop combo is regularly $470.

articles.title_orig: U.K. charges 2 men arrested over alleged Iran-linked terror plot against RAF Fairford air base used by U.S.
articles.title_zh: U.K. charges 2 men arrested over alleged Iran-linked terror plot against RAF Fairford air base used by U.S.
articles.content_orig:
British prosecutors said on Tuesday they had charged two British nationals under the National Security Act over an incident last month at the RAF Fairford airbase, with police saying the two were suspected of assisting Iran.
RAF Fairford had been used by US B-1 bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they were withdrawn on security grounds shortly after five men were arrested outside the military base in southwest England in the early hours of September 27.
The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday it had charged Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, with engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service.
Nouman Essghir, 24, was charged with one offense of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on August 22. The pair, who both live in London, will appear at Westminster Magistrate’s Court later on Tuesday.
Five other men arrested in connection with the case remain on police bail.
Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of national counter terrorism policing in the UK, said police believed the country Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran.
“We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the director general of Mi5 (the UK’s domestic security service) said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” Taylor added.
Initially the police arrested five men “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act” and explosives offenses near the Fairford airbase that has long used by the US Air Force. The men were then released on bail, which Taylor on Tuesday acknowledged “sparked significant questions and speculation about the investigation and why that was the case.”
“We know that decisions made during our investigations can sometimes appear illogical to those on the outside, but I want to make it very clear, that there will always be good reason, or rationale behind them,” he added. “Like our adversaries, our tactics vary – and may not always be obvious.”
Taylor said the decision to initially release the men “led to swifter progress, better evidence and ultimately us securing the charges.”
Earlier this month, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was “almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.” Iran has firmly rejected the accusations.
US President Donald Trump praised the arrest of the men at the time, telling reporters that the US had worked with Britain and that the men arrested were planning to do “big damage” to RAF Fairford.
“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump said. US intelligence had tracked planning by Iranian groups to target US assets at the base weeks ahead of any arrests, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
Days after the initial arrests, the US moved all of its long-range bombers from RAF Fairford following an unspecified threat, a knowledgeable source said.
At the time, Trump and Vice President JD Vance hinted that a threat against US assets had prompted the move.
“I think we can say that — I mean, they didn’t fly out by accident,” Trump said. “There were some threats, and rather than tempting the enemy, we’ll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit.”
Vance said the move was made “out of an abundance of caution,” suggesting it was a response to a potential threat from Iran even as he declined to detail the specific concerns.
CNN’s Billy Stockwell contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
A ​missing climber has been found dead after a drastic fall while descending from the summit of a Himalayan peak in north-east Nepal .
Wolfgang Waschiczek, a 57-year-old German man, had topped the 6,814 metre (22,256 ft) Ama Dablam peak on Sunday, but fell more than 1,500 metres (4,920 ⁠feet) on his way ​back ⁠down from the summit.
His body was recovered by search and rescue officials on Monday, Gokul Thapa, head of ⁠the Real Himalaya Pvt Ltd company, ​which ⁠provided local logistics to ‌him, said.
"His body was recovered by a search team today itself," Thapa told Reuters ‌from Lukla, gateway to ‌the mountainous region.
He added that the German had last been seen alive at Camp III on the mountain, and his body was spotted at 4,500m - a fall of about 1,700 metres.
Mr Waschiczek had shared the Ama Dablam expedition permit with Snowy Horizon, a trekking company. Its managing director Bodhraj Bhandari said the climber had lost contact with his guide at around 8am on October 26 while they prepared to descend the slope.
He and guide Sonam Lama had scaled the peak on Sunday and headed back down to Camp III that same evening.
“The pair decided to stay at Camp III overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” said Mr Bhandari.
The next morning, Mr Lama had asked the climber to wait with his safety gear while he returned the sleeping bag to its owner.
When he got back to their meeting point, Mr Waschiczek was nowhere to be seen.
“When Lama returned within less than five minutes, Wolfgang was not at the spot where he had been asked to wait with his safety gear,” added Mr Bhandari.
A helicopter and rescue team were alerted, and quickly began to search for the German, who was not wearing crampons on the snowy slope.
Sadly, his body was found nearly 2km below the camp.
It is the first casualty on Ama Dablam this season, a popular mountain among climbers in Solukhumbu district, home to the world's ⁠tallest peak, Mount Everest .
More than ‌300 mountaineers have ⁠received permits to climb Ama Dablam during ⁠the current September-November autumn climbing season.
Mr Thapa said the body of the German climber had been picked up from the mountain and would be carried by a ‌helicopter to a hospital in Kathmandu for ​a post mortem examination.
It comes just days after two Japanese climbers died on another peak in west Nepal after going missing.
A slab avalanche is believed to have swept them to their deaths, after heavy snowfall in the region.
Earlier this year, ‌10 climbers ​including a noted Nepali-British climber ‌died on a ​mountain in Pakistan.

articles.title_orig: China’s fifth plenum focuses on discipline and loyalty to Xi
articles.title_zh: China’s fifth plenum focuses on discipline and loyalty to Xi
articles.content_orig:
Plenums are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year
A major political gathering is under way in the Chinese capital, with a closed-door meeting of senior figures that could shape the look of the ruling Communist Party in the years to come.
The Fifth Plenum brings together around 300 members of the Central Committee and state media said it would pave the way for a "tightening of discipline" within the Party's ranks.
The four-day session that started on Monday will give Xi Jinping an opportunity to further consolidate his grip on power following recent purges.
The normally annual plenums are highly secretive, but a summary of decisions and a more detailed document will be made public after.
They are essentially closed door meetings of the Party's central committee that happen at least once a year.
There are usually seven plenums during each five-year Central Committee term and they are watched from afar because they are meant to signal the leadership's priorities.
The timing for this year's gathering is important because it is a year away from the next Party Congress, where a new set of priorities is set up and a new central committee appointed.
Officially, the Central Committee selects the Party's top leadership but the real processes leading to the selection are kept secret within the Party elite.
The next Party Congress will almost certainly reappoint Xi as the country's leader, following the abolition of term limits.
Past plenum sessions have been used to declare Xi as "the core" of the Party, abolish term limits which cleared the way for him to remain in power indefinitely, and elevate his personal philosophy â branded as "Xi Jinping Thought" â to the same level as Chairman Mao.
This year's plenum is an opportunity for Xi to dictate strategy in the run up to the Congress, ensuring that views are aligned and delegates loyal.
Even the location of the meeting, which will wrap up on Thursday, has not been announced. Past plenums have been held inside Beijing's Jingxi Hotel.
According to a readout from the powerful 21-member Politburo this September,  the plenum will adopt a decision on "several major issues persistently advancing the comprehensive strict governance of the Party", which is being read as a way to further ensure obedience and effectiveness from distant party officials.
This means it would also be a time of nervousness for delegates as they look around the room with its "empty chairs" following the scale of recent purges within the Party.
Allegations of corruption, even "moral corruption", have seen large swathes of senior figures culled.
"Moral corruption" has been seen by experts as a way of cracking down on perceived disloyalty to Xi because overall disloyalty to the Party can be interpreted as a breach of "morality".
The Asia Society Policy Institute has estimated that of 44 military members appointed to the Central Committee in 2022 only two have not been taken down.
The all-powerful seven-man Central Military Commission, which runs the armed forces in China, has also been whittled down to only two people, Xi Jinping and one other general.
This plenum is an opportunity for him to appoint new officers to this body.

articles.title_orig: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17
articles.title_zh: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17
articles.content_orig:
DETROIT — General Motors plans to transfer shares of its common stock from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq as the automaker attempts to position itself more as a technology-focused company.
The Detroit automaker said Tuesday that it expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq -listed company on Nov. 17. Its ticker symbol is expected to remain "GM," the company said.
"GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM CFO Paul Jacobson said in a release. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy."
GM noted the move will provide eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index .
Current shareholders do not need to take any action with respect to the transfer, the company said.
The switch marks a notable loss for the NYSE, as GM first listed on the exchange in 1911. The Detroit automaker also relisted on the stock exchange in 2010 following a government-backed bankruptcy.
GM follows other companies such as Walmart , DoorDash and Palantir Technologies that have transferred from the more traditional NYSE to the historically technology focused Nasdaq in recent years. Hilton Worldwide Holdings last week also announced plans to move trading from the NYSE to Nasdaq.
The key drivers for a listing transfer differ from company to company, but the Nasdaq in 2024 said common reasons include "index inclusion opportunities, cost effective fee structure, brand visibility partnership, access to Nasdaq's event space, and Nasdaq's suite of investor relations and ESG products."
GM's decision comes a week after the automaker held a technology-focused event where executives laid out the company's roadmap for artificial intelligence and self-driving vehicle technologies.
Shares of GM, which has been aggressively buying back stock , have more than doubled since 2024. GM's stock closed Monday at $76.31 per share. The company's market cap is roughly $64.4 billion.

articles.title_orig: Man charged with assisting ‘foreign intelligence service’ after incident at UK base used for Iran strikes
articles.title_zh: Man charged with assisting ‘foreign intelligence service’ after incident at UK base used for Iran strikes
articles.content_orig:
The U.K. has said it had charged a man with an offense of assisting a "foreign intelligence service" over an incident at a military base used by the U.S. for strikes on Iran.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, has been charged under the country's National Security Act "following an incident involving RAF Fairford," an air base in west England, prosecutors announced on Tuesday .
Between Aug. 31 and Sept. 28, Abdulkarim is alleged to have engaged in "conduct that would likely materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities", the Crown Prosecution Service added. The foreign country was not named.
Prosecutors also charged 24-year-old Nouman Essghir with "entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK".
The men are due to appear in court in London on Tuesday.
Five people were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses near RAF Fairford on Sept. 28. The base had been used as the U.S. Air Force's command outpost for operations from Europe and for American strikes on Iranian missile sites.
Announcing the charges, Frank Ferguson, a chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said that they followed "a Counter Terrorism Policing investigation into a high-profile incident involving RAF Fairford."
"We will continue to work closely with our partners as this complex investigation continues," he said.
After the arrests, U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. had moved its long-range bombers out of the U.K. in response to a threat "linked to Iran."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham told lawmakers earlier this month that the incident was "highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard."
Over the summer, Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned it saw any military base involved in launching airstrikes on Iran as a legitimate target.
Tehran denied any involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford.

articles.title_orig: An underground network of tunnels was discovered under Liverpool. Now workers think they’ve solved the mystery
articles.title_zh: An underground network of tunnels was discovered under Liverpool. Now workers think they’ve solved the mystery
articles.content_orig:
It’s an unassuming entrance to what’s been described as the world’s largest underground folly, a centuries-old mystery buried at least 60 feet below the streets of Liverpool, England, and stretching out for perhaps a square mile or more.
The peeling, graffiti-covered facade of a Georgian house is all that remains at ground level, the front wall propped up by steel beams and the unglazed windows framing blue rectangles of sky.
A small plaque on the wall’s left side declares that this is the former home of Joseph Williamson (1769-1840), “The Mole of Edge Hill,” and that the property is in the care of The Friends of Williamson Tunnels.
Our Sunday morning tour group gathers at a construction trailer on what is a working excavation site, to put on hard hats and yellow high-vis jackets.
We’re about to enter one of England’s most unusual tourist attractions: a multi-level network of tunnels and chambers , dug on the instructions of tobacco merchant Joseph Williamson in the early 19th century, and built under his home and the surrounding neighborhood
The tunnels were filled in with rubble and debris and lost to the world for more than a century, before being rediscovered at the turn of the 21st century, and then painstakingly excavated.
The decades-long mission of volunteer diggers, including our tour guide Tom Stapledon, has been to answer one question: Why were they built?
Wild theories have sprung up over the years, from them being used for the smuggling of contraband, to being the headquarters of an apocalyptic cult.
“We have struggled for 30 years with our research, trying to make sense of the story, and it’s very difficult because he was a very secretive man, and what he was doing was very strange and very eccentric,” says Stapledon as we prepare to make our descent.
They have finally landed, however, on what they believe is a solid theory. “If you can find more information that’s better than what we’ve got, then good luck to you.”
Workers have uncovered a hidden maze of 19th-century tunnels stretching 60 feet below Edge Hill, Liverpool. The challenge is now to find out why they were built.
We walk over to the Paddington site, the largest of the dozen or so known sections of the tunnels to be uncovered.
“We were searching for a way into the long-lost cellar system below these long-lost buildings in 1999” and with the help of construction workers building student housing on the site next door, “we managed to find a way to get in,” says Stapledon.
We climb down by ladder into the first of a series of large chambers hand-carved from the local sandstone and meticulously finished with vaulted brickwork ceilings. It’s dry, well-lit, and altogether comfortable, like an elegant wine cellar.
Portraits of Williamson and his wife Elizabeth — he a round-faced man with a quizzical stare, she with a soft expression and cloud of silver hair — greet us at the end of the room.
Williamson was born in Yorkshire but moved to Liverpool at the age of 11 to train as a tobacco merchant under Elizabeth’s father, Richard Tate. Williamson took over the business in 1803, having amassed considerable wealth through this and other ventures. He and Elizabeth remained childless, however, with no heirs to whom they could pass their fortune.
It quickly becomes apparent that calling this labyrinth “the Williamson tunnels” does this underground world a disservice. From this chamber alone, we have three onward routes : a pitch-black narrow cul-de-sac reminiscent of a prehistoric burial chamber, steps leading down into more chambers below, and the one we opt for first, into a room filled with displays of 19th- and 20th-century crockery, bottles and creepy little doll heads.
These are all finds from the excavation work that began when the tunnels were rediscovered in the 1990s. The items on display — and even the tunnels themselves — give us a window into the past.
In the early 19th century, Liverpool was a booming maritime city, although its wealth stayed with the merchant class and casual work was often a hard-scrabble life around the docks. It was a time of mass unemployment, as the mechanization of the Industrial Revolution put artisans out of work and the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815 brought in a wave of decommissioned soldiers.
The grandeur of the city’s history can still be seen in the epic sweep of Liverpool’s wide public spaces and spectacular diversity of architecture from the Georgian era onwards. When Joseph Williamson bought land in Edge Hill in 1806, it was with an eye to creating a well-to-do suburb in what was then an undeveloped area some two or three miles from the city.
He built “houses all along this street. But he was also quarrying out the sandstone because it’s solid, good hard red sandstone under our feet everywhere here,” explains Stapledon. “And he spent 34 years up here having his men digging out the sandstone and building houses over the top in many cases.”
This decades-long building project was, however, conducted in complete secrecy. Williamson never spoke of his plans publicly, was never known to invite anybody to see what was happening, and left no written records or maps that might shed light on the tunnels’ purpose or even their extent.
“The men who worked for him were presumably” instructed to maintain silence and “what was happening underground was only discovered a few years after he died,” says Stapledon.
“A few years after that, it all got filled up with rubbish and demolition material from the buildings up above, and it was all forgotten about and slipped into folk memory.”
Interest was revived just over a century ago after a series of articles by the historian Charles Hand was the catalyst for official surveys being carried out in 1926.
What it’s like inside the secret World War II tunnels set to become a huge new tourist attraction
The Joseph Williamson Society was founded in 1989, giving rise eventually, and somewhat confusingly, to the two separate groups preserving the site today.
There are the Friends of Williamson Tunnels (FoWT) and, just down the road in stableyards built after the merchant’s death, is the Williamson Tunnels Heritage Centre .
FoWT has by far the more impressive range of sites and the lengthier tour, but its rival boasts a small visitor center. With both operations offering tours at different times, a completist can maximize their experience by visiting both.
Of all the tunnel sites that have been identified and uncovered, the most spectacular by far is the FoWT’s 27-foot-high “Banqueting Hall.”
We enter this cathedral-like space from the top level, descending the scaffolding steps to explore the 65-foot-long expanse below, our voices echoing up to the gothic arch above.
The floor we stand on isn’t even a floor but a layer of dense rubble that the Friends of Williamson Tunnels estimates might be 20 feet deep at its thickest. The excavations in this room alone have been decades of painstaking labor by the volunteers.
The banqueting hall earns its name from a likely apocryphal tale that Williamson had once invited well-to-do guests to his home but served them a humble meal of bacon and beans. After many left in disgust, it was claimed he then treated the loyal visitors to a grand feast in a banqueting hall.
“Our source for a lot of the larger-than-life stories about Williamson is a fella called John Stonehouse,” who was what we’d today call “a pop historian,” says tour guide and volunteer Billy Moran, while leading a tour of the double and triple-decker tunnels at the Williamson Tunnels Heritage Centre.
These stories range from claims that he attended church with a horse whose hooves he set upon his own shoulders (a mind-boggling feat of interspecies acrobatics), to a colorful encounter with railway workers engaged in building what is now the West Coast Main Line from Liverpool to London, which cuts through the Edge Hill site.

articles.title_orig: Two British Men Charged Over Major Security Incident at U.K. Air Base
articles.title_zh: Two British Men Charged Over Major Security Incident at U.K. Air Base
articles.content_orig:
Oct. 27 (UPI) -- Authorities in Britain on Tuesday charged a 24-year-old man with spying for a foreign intelligence service, allegedly Iran, in relation to an incident at RAF Fairford in September in which a group of masked men in vans were arrested by counter-terrorism police near the base in the middle of the night.
The Crown Prosecution Service said in a news release that Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim of London was charged under the National Security Act with assisting a foreign intelligence service by carrying out activities in Britain between Aug. 31 and Sept. 28 "likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service."
"In this case, we believe that country to be Iran ," said Head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor.
A second man, Nouman Essghir, 24 and also from London, was charged with a single National Security offense that on Aug. 22 he entered, scoped out or got too close to a prohibited place "for a purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court later on Tuesday.
Five others arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses during the alleged Sept. 27 incident in the Gloucestershire village of Whelford, a half mile from the base, and then re-arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, are free on police bail, Counter Terrorism Policing said.
CTP added that an eighth man, a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian national who was re-arrested last week, has been released without charge but remains on strict police bail.
"We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the Director General of MI5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat," said CTP Assistant Commissioner Taylor.
RAF Fairford had been used by the U.S. military to fly missions amid its war with Iran.
A week after the security incident, the United States pulled out all of its bomber aircraft -- at least a dozen long-range B-1s -- stationed at the base, citing "threats."

articles.title_orig: Asian Stocks to Gain as Anthropic Files for IPO: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Asian Stocks to Gain as Anthropic Files for IPO: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_orig: Porsche profit rebounds as luxury carmaker reduces exposure to China
articles.title_zh: Porsche profit rebounds as luxury carmaker reduces exposure to China
articles.content_orig:
German sports carmaker Porsche said it has significantly reduced its exposure to China as operating profit rebounded in the first nine months of the year despite falling revenue and vehicle deliveries.
The Volkswagen-owned company published its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, announcing that operating profit was 1.74 billion euros ($1.94 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 40 million euros at the same time last year, when it booked around 2.7 billion euros in strategic restructuring costs.
Meanwhile, sales revenue fell 5.9% to 25.28 billion euros, while deliveries continued to decline, down 16% to 178,532. North America remained Porsche's largest sales region by volume.
China has historically been an important market for German luxury automakers, but they have struggled with growing competition from domestic brands, particularly in electric vehicles.
Porsche's China sales have fallen sharply in recent years amid intensifying competition from brands such as BYD, Geely and Xiaomi.
"Our geographically balanced sales footprint continues to provide resilience across different markets," Jochen Breckner, Porsche's chief financial officer, said in the earnings webcast on Tuesday.
"As you know, we have significantly reduced our exposure to China. This makes our overall business less dependent on developments from this challenging market environment."
Porsche shares were last seen trading 2.3% higher.
Porsche is also cutting thousands of jobs as part of a broader restructuring aimed at reducing costs and responding to weaker demand.
Citi analysts said in a note Tuesday that Porsche's first-nine-month results were as expected, despite challenges including China.
"Despite challenging conditions, including exceptionally low deliveries, higher costs, and higher battery electric vehicle deliveries, Porsche's underlying EBIT remains very resilient and ahead of German premium peers," the analysts said.
They added that Porsche has laid out a plan to return to double-digit underlying operating profit margins, with recovery expected to start in 2028, and net cash flow expected to rebound to above its IPO levels by 2031.
"Whilst FY27 will remain a trough year, we still see a solid, well-supported and credible multi-year EBIT and net cash recovery starting financial year 2028 - unlike many peers," the analysts said.

articles.title_orig: Ghost Of Yotei Was A Hit, But Its Developer Is Reportedly Cutting Jobs
articles.title_zh: Ghost Of Yotei Was A Hit, But Its Developer Is Reportedly Cutting Jobs
articles.content_orig:
Layoffs have become a kind of boogeyman over the gaming industry, constantly talked about, but always appearing out of nowhere when they do arrive. While the heads of these companies might have careful plans, the sudden loss of a job can hit even the most hopeful dev at the worst time.
Sometimes, the timing feels almost cruel, as with Sucker Punch's recent hit reported to Aftermath. Per a recently released member of Sucker Punch, the studio is cutting 26 positions right after the release of Ghost of Yōtei's Complete Edition re-release. What should feel like a victory lap for the team has suddenly turned grim, with employees inside the studio and those looking in equally confused by the decision.
In the current industry, it almost feels like quality doesn't matter, at least internally to the big shots making company-wide decisions. After Ghost of Yōtei's phenomenal release earlier this year, making it the best-selling Sony title of 2026, the Complete Edition seemed to be the standard re-release fare, with all the DLC included and a few adjustments made.
Despite what should have been a lower-budget, big-win bonus project just dropping, Sucker Punch leadership cut the positions after "carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project." The current upcoming project from Sucker Punch is unknown, but the team is rattled, with nothing but a promise of more info coming in the following weeks.
​​​​​​ What should feel like a victory lap for the team has suddenly turned grim, with employees inside the studio and those looking in equally confused by the decision.
Sucker Punch itself is small when compared to other AAA studios, coming up at only about 200 active employees before the recent firings. Losing 1/8 of the entire team is a major hit, and makes little sense when apparently approaching plans for an all-new title. This makes Sucker Punch another mark on the road of successful teams deemed too expensive to maintain, a frustrating sentiment in current gaming.
Whether studios are willing to take similar hits for late-stage victories, the constant eagerness to cut the ground out from under devs feels incredibly shortsighted, putting both new blood and established experts on their butts in a very tumultuous time of the year. I imagine many at Sucker Punch had hoped earning so well for one of the biggest names in gaming would earn them a little security, but if XBOX's constant cutting of their own staff is any indication, there really is no safety in success.
I'm not sure if devs have ever really had it harder across the board in the industry, but the current waves of layoffs and studio closures feel never-ending. Despite how easy it would be to stick our heads in the sand and give up, every day is giving us little victories to focus on. The #SaveMassEffect initiative, for one, has become massive, gathering over 200,000 signatures over the course of just one week.
Alongside the roaring support in BioWare's corner, smaller teams like Uchikoshi's newly founded CRASH KEYS are getting the exact support from the gaming public they need to get their foot in the door, a real feel-good story when needed most. The voices of players really do matter, and putting those voices into action can do genuine wonders for both player satisfaction and the health of the industry.
With how big gaming has become, we should be seeing more studios, constant titles, and those can be found if you're willing to step back from the blinding spotlights of AAA. Like any creative industry, you can find artists making exactly what you'd love to see constantly, and nothing is more satisfying than watching a small team or individual improve their title over time.
As long as they're given support both internally and from fans, the talented individuals released from Sucker Punch can absolutely hit the ground running, with plenty of studios and teams eager to snatch up their skills.
